title: More sightings, more observers
bodyMd:
A volunteer wildlife project reported a rise in moth sightings after launching a mobile application. The app simplified submission and recruited many new participants, especially in towns. Some commentators interpreted the larger sighting total as evidence that moth populations had recovered. Project scientists were more cautious. A count of reports combines the abundance of organisms with the effort and skill of observers. More observers can produce more reports even when the underlying population is unchanged.

The scientists did not discard the new records. Instead, they separated repeatedly monitored sites from newly enrolled sites and recorded the duration of each observation session. They also compared trends in common, easily recognised species with those in species requiring specialist identification. These adjustments could not remove every source of bias, but they made it possible to ask whether increased sightings persisted after plausible changes in observation effort were considered.
